text: Copper Prices Fall as US Election Clouds AI Demand and Tariff Outlook Copper prices dropped to their lowest level since July, falling as much as 1.5% to around $13,642 per ton on the London Metal Exchange. The decline reflects growing concerns that political changes in the US could weaken two major drivers of copper demand: expanding AI infrastructure investment and the possibility of higher US import tariffs. A broader selloff in technology stocks has also increased risk aversion across industrial metals markets. The Democratic Party’s control of Congress has reduced expectations of aggressive US copper tariffs, potentially easing the price premium on American copper and encouraging metal flows back into global markets. Concerns about slowing AI-related investment and tighter financial conditions are adding further pressure. However, physical copper markets continue to show supply tightness, with domestic Chinese copper premiums rising above 2,500 yuan per ton, their highest level since records began in 2015.

text: Treasury Traders Bet on Bond Rally Ahead of US Jobs Report US Treasury traders are positioning for further gains in government bonds ahead of the October employment report, as expectations of additional Federal Reserve interest-rate hikes continue to weaken. A global stock market selloff has boosted demand for safe-haven assets, pushing Treasury yields to their lowest levels since early September, with the 10-year yield at 4.82%. Some options traders are betting that yields could fall further, potentially reaching 4.7% or even 4.35% in the coming weeks. Investors expect October nonfarm payrolls to increase by 65,000, compared with September’s 29,000 gain. However, even stronger-than-expected employment data may not derail the bond rally, as many investors are prepared to buy Treasuries if prices decline. Meanwhile, falling oil prices have eased inflation expectations, reducing pressure on the Fed to raise rates. Markets are now closely watching upcoming employment and inflation data ahead of the Fed’s December policy meeting.

author: firstsquaw
text: Oil Prices Fall as Hopes Grow for Middle East De-Escalation Oil prices declined as markets reacted to signs of renewed diplomatic efforts to reduce tensions in the Middle East. Brent crude fell below $98 per barrel after rising nearly 4% in the previous session, while US benchmark WTI traded around $90. Prices remain highly volatile amid uncertainty over the conflict and its impact on global oil supplies. Hopes for a diplomatic breakthrough increased after Qatar’s Emir discussed de-escalation efforts with US President Donald Trump. Iran is reportedly reviewing proposals from mediators regarding its nuclear programme, but significant disagreements remain. Tehran is demanding the removal of the US naval blockade, sanctions relief and the release of frozen assets before fully reopening the Strait of Hormuz, a critical route for global oil shipments.
